However, the accurate retrieval of these attributes, including target class, location, and size, is challenging due to the highly nonlinear relationships between the received signals and different attributes. In addition, new beamforming strategies are also required to balance multi-user communication and semantic sensing performance. To address the first challenge, we develop a physics-guided inference model that leverages signal propagation priors and a unified Transformer backbone to effectively characterize the highly nonlinear relationships between received ISAC signals and multiple attributes. As for the second challenge, we develop a multi-stage training framework for the optimization of beamformers and model parameters, aiming to improve semantic sensing performance while guaranteeing multi-user communication requirements. Simulation results show that under the same multi-user communication rate requirements, the proposed scheme can provide more than 12% performance gains across classification, localization, and size estimation tasks compared with existing methods and achieve 91.21% classification accuracy using only two OFDM frames, demonstrating the feasibility of accurate semantic sensing with low measurement overhead.

nominations.title: DBFM: Dual-Band Flow Matching for ECG Super-Resolution
nominations.authors: Fan-Yi Hsu, Kuan-Chen Wang, I Chiu, Kai-Chun Liu, Ping-Cheng Yeh, Yu Tsao
nominations.abstract: Long-term ECG monitoring is increasingly supported by wearable and portable devices, where limited power and transmission capacity motivate acquisition at lower sampling rates. ECG super-resolution (SR) aims to reconstruct high-sampling-rate signals from low-sampling-rate recordings for clinical analysis. A recent diffusion-based approach, DiSR-ECG, has demonstrated powerful reconstruction performance, particularly in cross-dataset evaluation. However, its iterative sampling during inference incurs high computational cost when processing large volumes of long-term ECG data. To reduce this cost while maintaining reconstruction accuracy, we propose Dual-Band Flow Matching (DBFM), a generative framework for ECG SR. DBFM decomposes ECG signals into low- and high-frequency components and separately learns their source-to-target transport using conditional flow matching. This dual-band formulation enables frequency-specific reconstruction, while one-step inference substantially reduces computational complexity. Experimental results show that DBFM achieves performance comparable to or better than DiSR-ECG while reducing inference FLOPs by approximately 98.7\%. These results demonstrate that DBFM enables computationally efficient ECG SR without compromising reconstruction quality.

nominations.title: Dual-Pilot Design for OCDM Channel Estimation
nominations.authors: Ayoub Ammar Boudjelal, Huseyin Arslan
nominations.abstract: Channel acquisition in orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) over doubly-dispersive channels incurs a large pilot overhead, since delay and Doppler jointly shift the symbols in the chirp domain and separating them requires repeated pilots, each protected against the complete coupled displacement. This letter proposes a dual-pulsone pilot design that reduces this overhead in two steps. First, a pulsone occupies fewer chirp-domain bins than alias-free Doppler estimation requires, deliberately allowing Doppler wrapping. Second, a phase-offset pulsone is placed within the same protected region to observe a complementary part of the displacement, further reducing the shared guard. The phase offset also resolves the wrapping ambiguity, enabling low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Simulations show competitive estimation and BER performance, with the lowest complexity and highest payload efficiency among the considered OCDM estimators.

nominations.title: Interference-Free In-Symbol Pilots for High-Mobility DFT-s-OFDM Uplink
nominations.authors: Ayoub Ammar Boudjelal, Huseyin Arslan
nominations.abstract: The 5G New Radio (NR) uplink uses discrete Fourier transform spread orthogonal frequency-division multi- plexing (DFT-s-OFDM) for its low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Its demodulation reference signal (DMRS) occupies whole symbols, although channel estimation only needs channel samples. Since existing designs cannot place pilots inside a data symbol without interference on the data, or on both data and pilots, NR keeps whole DMRS symbols, which wastes spectral efficiency (SE), and adds more of them as the channel varies faster, lowering the SE further. We develop a technique that places pilots free of data interference inside the data symbols, for frequency-domain channel estimation in every symbol. Using the Zak transform, we show that leaving a set of equally spaced pre- DFT samples empty frees one column of the Zak grid of the DFT output. The data values of the pilot subcarriers are relocated into this column by adding a constant over a few subcarrier combs, which preserves the energy and keeps the NR DFT sizes. The receiver undoes it linearly with comb sums, without decisions or side information, and a symbol loses as few as one data sample beyond its pilots. Since the pilots raise the PAPR, we keep them few per symbol and hop their positions across symbols, so that a two-dimensional estimator over the slot resolves long delay spreads at high Doppler. On 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels, pilots in every symbol achieve a higher effective SE than all NR DMRS configurations from pedestrian to high- speed-train velocities, at a PAPR close to plain DFT-s-OFDM.

nominations.title: Waveform Randomization for Secure ISAC Against Informed Eavesdroppers
nominations.authors: Zexin Fang, Bin Han, Shuangyang Li, Hans D. Schotten
nominations.abstract: We study waveform-level protection of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) against a UAV-mounted eavesdropper (Eve) that knows the waveform construction and the phase-key generation rules. The novelty of this work is a systematic, budget-explicit attack analysis: instead of relying on undisclosed design details, we quantify what an informed Eve can learn and reconstruct, and how much computation this takes. We protect the sensing reference with Fourier-curve modulation, phase keys, and tangent Artificial Noise (AN), with burst- specific information shared over secure backhaul. We compare three key-generation rules against offline Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based sequence identification and online Adam and phase-aware expectation-maximization (EM) key recovery, under complete or partial nominal-sequence knowledge. A power- domain model couples residual key error with imperfect AN removal and predicts coherent delay locking. Results show that reusable key structure permits sequence identification even when demodulation fails, position-dependent keying raises recovery difficulty, and seed-expanded keying resists the evaluated clas- sifier within the learning budget. Waveform simulations under multipath, clutter, and echo accumulation confirm the sensing impact.

nominations.title: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Forward Scatter Radar
nominations.authors: Abdollah Ajorloo, Stefano Amato Ciciretti, Fabiola Colone
nominations.abstract: Forward Scatter Radar (FSR) enhances the detection of low-observable targets by exploiting the increased radar cross section that occurs when a target crosses the transmitter-receiver baseline. Conventional FSR typically uses single-input single-output (SISO) architectures with limited localization capability, while recent single-input multiple-output (SIMO) systems enable non-coherent angular estimation. This paper introduces a multiple-input multiple-output FSR (MIMO-FSR) framework for joint estimation of target direction of departure (DoD) and direction of arrival (DoA) from non-coherent, amplitude-only measurements. By exploiting antenna arrays at both the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX), the proposed approach enables two-dimensional angular localization without phase synchronization among TX/RX array elements. We establish the underlying operating principle under ideal signal separability and then develop practical frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) and time-division multiplexing (TDM) implementations. For each scheme, dedicated signal models and processing methods compensate for distortions caused by frequency offsets and target motion, respectively. We also derive analytical expressions for angular resolution, ambiguity conditions, and output-map distortions. Extensive numerical simulations for short- and long-baseline scenarios reveal operational limits and trade-offs between the two multiplexing schemes. Finally, proof-of-concept outdoor experiments using software-defined radio platforms validate the proposed framework. The results demonstrate joint DoD-DoA estimation and support the feasibility of MIMO-FSR for future active, passive, and integrated sensing and communications applications.

nominations.title: A Hybrid Analytical-Neural Residual Surrogate for Fast Radio Propagation Prediction over Irregular Terrain
nominations.authors: Yongyuan Hu, Jiahao Li, Keqi Ni, Yuqi Ouyang, Hao Qin
nominations.abstract: Fast prediction of radio-wave propagation over irregular terrain is important for coverage analysis in mountainous environments, where many terrain and antenna configurations must be evaluated repeatedly. High-fidelity split-step parabolic equation (SSPE) solvers can capture terrain-induced shadowing and interference, but their computational cost is high for repeated planning studies. Learning-based surrogates reduce this cost, but direct field regression asks the network to learn both analytically tractable propagation trends and terrain-dependent residual structure. This paper proposes a hybrid analytical-neural residual surrogate that separates these two parts. A deterministic analytical baseline represents free-space spreading, antenna directivity, modified knife-edge diffraction, and terrain-aware specular reflection, while a compact coarse-to-fine neural network predicts the residual field. The network uses baseline-derived guidance channels, anisotropic convolutions, and feature-wise antenna conditioning to match the directional structure of terrain propagation fields. On synthetic SSPE data at 1.0 GHz, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 2.1061 dB, compared with 3.3955 dB for a standard U-Net and 3.2560 dB for a reproduced physics-guided CNN, while reducing the average inference time to 11.30 ms per sample. A zero-shot test at 1.8 GHz gives an MAE of 2.8692 dB without retraining, and a case study on the measured Hjorringvej terrain profile shows that the prediction remains consistent with the SSPE reference and follows the measured path-loss trend.

nominations.title: Robust inverse dielectric design of skin phantoms for implantable wireless link evaluation
nominations.authors: Andreas Prokscha, Ali Alhaj Abbas, Samar Elmaadawy, Mandana Jalali, Yamen Zantah, Josep M. Jornet, Daniel Erni, Thomas Kaiser
nominations.abstract: Skin phantoms support reproducible evaluation of implantable wireless links, yet published complex permittivities of skin predict different propagation losses. We formulate a robust inverse design to determine a homogeneous phantom permittivity that minimizes the largest channel-loss difference across selected skin reference models, incidence angles and both transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic polarizations. Computed candidates and analytical lower bounds bracket the optimal mismatch and constrain the critical depth. Across seven frequencies from 5 to 500 GHz, the minimax mismatch at 1.3 mm ranges from 1.13 to 13.72 dB. For a 3 dB tolerance, suitable permittivities exist at every investigated depth at 5 GHz, while critical depths at the other frequencies range from 0.23 to 1.01 mm. Only one of seven material cases from the literature meets a 6 dB tolerance at 1.3 mm. These results translate channel-loss tolerances into quantitative design criteria for skin phantoms used in implantable wireless link evaluation.

nominations.title: Embodied Intelligence for Spectrum Map Construction in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
nominations.authors: Hongtao Liang, Yiyao Wan, Jiahuan Ji, Lingda Meng, Fuhui Zhou, Qihui Wu
nominations.abstract: Accurate spectrum map construction by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for intelligent resource management in low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs). Although various construction approaches have been investigated, their performance often degrades under extremely sparse sampling because purely data-driven models may not capture the underlying propagation physics. To address these challenges, an embodied intelligence framework is proposed, which synergistically integrates closed-loop perception-cognition-execution (PCE) coupling and embodied exploration to achieve precise and efficient spectrum construction. Based on this framework, a corresponding embodied cognition and decision network (ECDNet) with three tightly coupled modules is designed. Specifically, by leveraging distance-aware convolutions, the semantic bridge, and adaptive feature alignment mechanisms, ECDNet establishes the bidirectional information flow between construction and decision-making. Simulation results show that ECDNet achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.787 dBm at 4.00% sampling under the non-revisiting spiral protocol. Furthermore, a practical UAV-based spectrum construction platform is developed and field-deployed to provide prototype-level evidence that the sensing, cognition, and action modules execute as a closed loop on size, weight, and power constrained UAV edge devices.

nominations.title: QoS-Constrained Sum-Rate Maximization in RIS-Assisted Pinching-Antenna NOMA Systems
nominations.authors: L\"utfullah \"Ozkan, Saliha B\"uy\"uk\c{c}orak
nominations.abstract: This paper investigates a two-user downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system jointly assisted by a single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) and a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). To maximize the achievable sum rate under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints, the pinching antenna (PA) positions, RIS phase shifts, and power allocation coefficients are jointly optimized. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is addressed using an alternating optimization (AO) framework, where power allocation is obtained in closed form, while RIS phase shifts and PA positions are optimized through majorization-minimization (MM) and sequential quadratic programming (SQP), respectively. Numerical results show that the proposed architecture achieves higher sum rates than conventional-antenna and PASS-only benchmarks. Moreover, the MM- and SQP-based optimization stages achieve performance comparable to semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and grid-based exhaustive search, respectively, while the AO algorithm exhibits rapid convergence.

nominations.title: A Causal Schr\"odinger-Newton Theory that Conserves Energy and Momentum
nominations.authors: Daisuke Miki, Yanbei Chen, Yiqiu Ma, Yubao Liu, Selim M. Shahriar
nominations.abstract: This paper provides a theoretical justification for using the Causal-Conditional Schr\"odinger-Newton theory (CCSN) as a phenomenological model for classical gravity sourced by quantum matter. In CCSN, the gravitational field is driven not by expectation values in the global quantum state, but by conditional expectation values of the stress-energy tensor evaluated on local states determined by measurement records in the causal past. Because these local states are defined operationally from measurement records, the formulation is independent of any particular interpretation of quantum measurement while leading to unambiguous phenomenological dynamics. We apply this framework to a self-gravitating optomechanical system under continuous measurement and show that the resulting stochastic Schr\"odinger evolution, augmented by a classical gravitational field sourced by local conditional stress-energy expectations, can be made consistent with energy-momentum conservation by introducing a corrector tensor. The corrector restores the conservation law without altering the leading Newtonian predictions of CCSN, contributing only negligible post-Newtonian corrections in current experimental regimes. These results place CCSN on firmer theoretical footing and clarify its role as a viable phenomenological model for ongoing and future tests of classical gravity coupled to quantum matter.

nominations.title: Physical Realization of the Luczka Model: Inducing Interaction and Entanglement Between Spins
nominations.authors: A. R. Kuzmak
nominations.abstract: The Luczka model describes the interaction of spins with a common bosonic environment in the pure-dephasing regime, in which the bosonic modes couple directly to only one spin component. Due to its specific form of interaction, the model is exactly solvable and has been widely used to describe spin decoherence and effective spin-spin interactions mediated by a common bosonic environment. However, to the best of our knowledge, its physical realization and the specific conditions under which such an interaction can be implemented have not yet been addressed. Here, we propose a physical realization of the Luczka spin-environment interaction by coupling the spin system to unidirectionally propagating, polarized electromagnetic radiation. In contrast to the original Luczka model, which allows an arbitrary angular distribution of photon wave vectors, our scheme gives a unidirectional photon flux with retaining a frequency distribution of the photons. As an illustrative application of the proposed realization, we investigate spin-entanglement dynamics for coherent, single-mode thermal, and Ohmic

nominations.title: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: From Nonlinear to Emergent and Solitonic Approaches
nominations.authors: Niko Brimi
nominations.abstract: This thesis investigates the role of nonlinearity in approaches beyond standard quantum mechanics, following a path from modifications of quantum dynamics to the possibility of an emergent statistical description. We first examine Weinberg's nonlinear formulation and its implications for the statistical interpretation of quantum states. We then discuss de Broglie-Bohm theory and the Madelung formulation, which provide a framework for comparing guided trajectories with ensemble descriptions involving momentum fluctuations. The Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty approach identifies the fluctuation energy associated with the quantum potential. We then investigate whether quantum dynamics can emerge from the collective statistics of solitons in a fluctuating background, using a Galilean formulation of the complex sine-Gordon model. Within a weak-noise approximation, we identify a regime in which the statistics of the soliton centres reproduce the Schr{\"o}dinger equation, with an effective action scale determined by the background fluctuations. This correspondence is established for Gaussian ensembles and potentials at most quadratic. These results provide a concrete setting for exploring how quantum dynamics can emerge as a statistical description of underlying nonlinear field dynamics.

nominations.title: A counterexample to the Ho-Hsieh VQCS saturation conjecture
nominations.authors: Edward Jiang
nominations.abstract: We show that there exists a 4-qubit state that can be prepared by a variational quantum-classical simulation (VQCS) circuit ansatz containing 3 layers, but not with 2 layers. This disproves the strong form of a conjecture presented by Ho and Hsieh stating that the expressivity of VQCS on $L$ qubits saturates at $L/2$ layers. The weak form of the conjecture concerning the preparation of the ground state remains open.

nominations.title: Certifying closed labs in device-independent tests of indefinite causality
nominations.authors: Hannah Seabrook, Fabio Costa, Paul Skrzypczyk, Giulia Rubino
nominations.abstract: Indefinite causal order allows processes in which the order of events is not predetermined, enabling information-processing advantages unattainable with fixed causal structures. A long-standing open problem is whether such processes can be certified without trusting the devices used to demonstrate them, analogous to device-independent certifications of Bell nonlocality. Causal inequalities offer a route towards this goal, since their violation is intended to rule out all definite causal structures. However, fully device-independent certification of indefinite causal order remains elusive. The difficulty lies in the closed laboratories assumption, which requires each party to interact at most once with systems that mediate communication. Without this assumption, ordinary two-way communication can reproduce causal-inequality violations without involving indefinite causal order. Yet an untrusted device could violate the assumption by interacting with the mediating system more than once, while remaining undetected from input-output statistics alone. We address this loophole by embedding a minimal set of additional experimental components into a certification scheme. These elements probabilistically probe the underlying process, enabling the closed laboratories assumption to be validated directly within the protocol. Our framework provides operationally meaningful minimal-assumption tests of indefinite causal order, clarifying its distinction from nonlocality and paving the way for cryptographic and self-testing applications.

nominations.title: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters
nominations.authors: Matteo Massaro, Adolfo del Campo
nominations.abstract: Quantum time crystals are states of matter that spontaneously break time translation symmetry, extending the notion of crystalline order to time. While their out-of-equilibrium version has been successfully realized by periodic driving, the equilibrium counterpart remains elusive. Here we introduce "ground-state chiral quantum clusters": self-bound many-body ground states supporting a persistent current. We provide a minimal field theory describing these states, and an exact microscopic realization via the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In the latter, the ground-state density-density correlator exhibits the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically disperses and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring, realizing persistent motion at equilibrium. Possible experimental probes are discussed.

nominations.title: Spinal reflected entropy reveals logical magic
nominations.authors: Zong-Yue Hou, Yuzhen Zhang, Zhi-Cheng Yang, Yingfei Gu
nominations.abstract: Entanglement and magic are usually regarded as independent quantum resources. Here we connect the two in the toric code, where the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy of the stored logical state, a widely used measure of magic, acquires a direct interpretation in terms of entanglement. We introduce the spinal reflected entropy, defined on a neighborhood of a spine of the underlying surface as the reflected entropy between a disk around the vertex of the spine and bands along its noncontractible loops. It obeys an area law with a topological correction and contains one additional term that carries all the dependence on the stored state. On a torus, this term equals the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy of the stored state plus the logarithm of the ground-state degeneracy. The mechanism is topological. On the surface sewn to its reflected copy, the bands close into tubes, logical Pauli operators become anyon charges threading them, and these charges are distributed as the outcomes of Bell sampling of the stored state. The result extends to surfaces of higher genus and to general two-dimensional topological stabilizer codes on qubits. Logical magic thus becomes a geometrically defined entanglement quantity, one that shallow circuits preserving the code space cannot change.

nominations.title: Quantum State Preparation from Nonreversible Markov Chains via Spectral Filtering
nominations.authors: Wael Drif
nominations.abstract: We develop a framework for preparing and transporting coherent quantum samples of nonreversible Markov chains. Our approach uses spectral filtering to construct state-dependent phase operations, which are combined with fixed-point amplitude amplification to transport quantum states along a sequence of related chains. We study two complementary constructions with different oracle requirements and target states. The first uses coherent access to both forward and time-reversed transitions and targets the stationary quantum sample, with a filtering cost governed by a multiplicative-reversibilization gap. The second requires only forward transitions and selects the leading eigenstate of a flat discriminant, which may differ from the stationary quantum sample; we quantify this bias under additional spectral and reversibility-on-average conditions. For the forward-only construction, we implement the spectral filter using generalized quantum signal processing with a single signal qubit, apart from transition registers and oracle workspace. We establish a common transport procedure and derive error and resource bounds that account for spectral properties, overlaps between successive selected states, and the costs of coherent multi-step transition oracles. Up to logarithmic factors, spectral-filter degrees scale inversely with the square roots of the relevant spectral gaps, while transport introduces an additional inverse-square-root dependence on certified lower bounds on squared overlaps between successive selected states. Our results extend existing nonreversible spectral methods to multistage coherent state transport with controlled approximation errors.

nominations.title: A Constraint-Preserving Preconditioned Quantum Solver for Heterogeneous Brinkman Flo
nominations.authors: Shreya Savadatti, Franz Franchetti
nominations.abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation can reduce the number of evaluations needed to estimate an average, but its advantage in PDE uncertainty quantification depends on the cost of each coherent solve. We study this problem for incompressible Brinkman flow through a porous material with spatially varying drag. We first express the velocity in divergence-free coordinates using a polar Riesz map, obtaining a positive-definite system that preserves incompressibility in the exact formulation. We then introduce a Sobolev--Riesz preconditioner and prove that the resulting condition number is bounded by $\alpha_{\max}/\alpha_{\min}$, independently of the grid resolution. We construct block encodings and reversible-arithmetic circuits for this formulation and show how to estimate the mean kinetic energy without reconstructing the full velocity field. By accounting for both sampling and solver costs, we establish conditions under which the method has a gate-complexity advantage over single-level classical grid-resolving solvers. Numerical experiments verify the conditioning bound and the accuracy of the circuit components at the tested sizes. The complexity advantage is conditional on the stated input and discretization assumptions; no quantum-hardware runtime advantage is demonstrated.

nominations.title: Quantum Control Under Control-Dependent Decoherence
nominations.authors: Cyril Morluyan Cordor, Anthony M. Bloch, Eitan Geva
nominations.abstract: Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on coherent control protocols. To this end, we examine the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on the controllability of an open quantum system in the case of a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath. We show that coherent controls wield greater influence on the dynamics of the system than predicted by a Lindblad-type equation that models decoherence as time- and control-independent.

nominations.title: Long-range effective interactions in a rectangular tight-binding lattice within the semiclassical approximation
nominations.authors: Evaristo Mamani, Diego Sanjines
nominations.abstract: We extend the semiclassical formalism of Dunlap--Kenkre (1986) and of Mamani et al. (2017) to obtain the effective Hamiltonian of a rectangular tight-binding lattice with interactions to all neighbors, in the presence of a rapidly oscillating field $\mathbf f(\omega t)$ and a static potential $V(x,y)$, both arbitrary, by means of: a canonical transformation, the semiclassical approximation and the Kapitza-type time-averaging techniques (Mamani 2017). At zeroth order in $1/\omega$, a field with even symmetry reparameterizes the hopping elements through factors in terms of Bessel functions. At order $1/\omega^2$, the induced hopping elements arise from the coupling between the oscillating field and the curvature of the static potential (its 2nd derivative). For fields $\mathbf f(\omega t)$ with odd symmetry, in addition to renormalizing the interactions, an effective band shift appears. For the two-dimensional lattice, we obtain the generalization of the exact dynamic localization condition of Dignam et al. (2002) and Domachuk et al. (2002), and we show that the resulting band-collapse is in general anisotropic --axial interactions are suppressed but some diagonal interactions persist--, so that exact dynamic localization in the stroboscopic sense is guaranteed only when the band-collapse is complete for all neighbors. Finally, we numerically identify an effective-duplication scenario for the rectangular lattice, associated with approximate solutions of a Pythagorean-type relation among zeros of the zeroth-order Bessel function.

nominations.title: Blueprint for DOE Quantum Supercomputing
nominations.authors: Ryan Bennink, Robin Blume-Kohout, Salman Habib, Andrew Landahl, Hai Ah Nam, Laura Schulz, Mallikarjun Shankar, Nicholas Wright
nominations.abstract: Quantum computing stands at the threshold of a transformative decade, where the field will evolve from small-scale demonstrations toward practical scientific computing at scale. This Blueprint identifies fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs) as a viable, scalable, and broadly applicable path to achieving "quantum scientific utility." It outlines a strategy to prepare the US Department of Energy (DOE) for FTQCs and their integration into the US national scientific computing infrastructure. Its purpose is to identify the steps, milestones, and research directions necessary for DOE to enable initial deployment of FTQCs in 2028 as a scientific tool for the nation and mature this capability into the 2030s. Given recent demonstrations of logical operations on error-corrected logical qubits and the advancement of commercial hardware roadmaps, DOE should begin preparations for large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computing deployment for DOE science missions. This Blueprint proposes that DOE focus on (1) deploying first-generation scientifically relevant quantum computers with at least 100 logical qubits and performing at least 10,000 to 100,000 hard logical operations in scientifically relevant calculations; (2) developing essential FTQC programming competencies, system software, and facility readiness; and (3) investing in cutting-edge focused R&D that fosters breakthroughs in scientific applications, algorithms, and logical architectures needed to accelerate the advent of scientific utility. This effort will position DOE to transition to larger systems: production-scale quantum computers that comprise 1,000 to 10,000 logical qubits, perform 1 to 10 billion hard logical operations, and execute scientifically useful computations at scale. The Blueprint calls for transformative R&D and collective action to accelerate the advent of scientific quantum utility and bring it within reach by 2028.

nominations.title: All-electronic geometric phase gate on Doppler-cooled trapped ions using an axial mode
nominations.authors: P. Rahimi, C. Knapp, P. Zantis, T. Maddock, S. J. Hile, J. Randall, M. Siegele-Brown, S. Weidt, W. K. Hensinger
nominations.abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of a high-fidelity oscillating magnetic gradient entangling gate on the axial stretch mode of a two-ion crystal in a micro-fabricated surface Paul trap, therefore allowing for mixed-species sympathetic cooling. With only Doppler-cooled $^{171}$Yb$^+$ ions at $\bar{n}$ = 50(5), we achieve Bell-state fidelities far above the relevant fault-tolerant threshold, simplifying transport protocols within a shuttling-based-architecture. The control fields consist only of an oscillating current applied to submerged integrated wires emitting a B-field gradient near-resonant with the axial mode, and resonant microwave pulses at the qubit frequency constituting very low gate calibration overheads. We also demonstrate an adiabatic elimination of spin-motion entanglement (AESE) version of the gate, showcasing significant robustness.

nominations.title: How Small Can a Single Shor Run Be? Limits and Constructions for secp256k1
nominations.authors: Yicheng Guang, Yuliang Xiong, Yueqi Chen, Xun Gao
nominations.abstract: Most resource estimates for breaking secp256k1 with Shor's algorithm describe one long run per attempt, and the spacetime volume of that run, its peak number of logical qubits times its Toffoli count, sets its logical-error budget. Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff shrinks each run by using more runs, but how far it can shrink the largest run, and at what circuit cost, has not been determined. We minimize the volume of the largest run while every key is recovered with probability at least 0.99, within ten times the total volume of three runs of H\"aner et al.\ and $2^{40}$ classical operations. We prove that a linear run fixed in advance, which starts its group register at a point and discards its label, reveals at most $\log_2(1+(|S|-1)/r)$ bits about a uniform key, where $|S|$ counts its exponent values and $r$ is the group order. With generic post-processing and the baseline's window costs, splitting alone then shrinks the largest run at most 1.86 times within the budget. To gain more, we make each exponent bit cheaper with windows that share one table point among exponent values related by six symmetries of the curve, on a point-addition core borrowed from the ECDSA.Fail leaderboard. One random scalar and one random start per run give every approximate addition uniform operands, and a bound on each run's outcomes certifies, for every key, a decoder that discards flagged runs. We count every Toffoli gate and every qubit of every run, and each configuration solved all 563 of its pre-registered simulated trials on secp256k1. The best one shrinks the largest run 3.87 times at 8.79 times the baseline's total volume, against 2.81 times for Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff on the same core, and its run is at least 2.6 times smaller than every design of Initio Intelligence.

nominations.title: Neural Decoding of Logical Clifford Circuits with Transversal Gates
nominations.authors: Yicheng Guang, Yuliang Xiong, Xun Gao, Yueqi Chen
nominations.abstract: On neutral-atom and trapped-ion machines, a transversal gate needs only one syndrome round, so a logical gate takes up to d times less time than with lattice surgery. However, transversal gates make decoding harder, because a transversal CNOT copies errors between two blocks of physical qubits, so a decoder must read all blocks of a circuit together. Algorithmic decoders for such circuits gain accuracy at the cost of speed. Neural decoders ease this trade-off, but they must infer from data where errors go across each gate and how logical outcomes propagate through the circuit, although both are known exactly. In this work, we present Duet, a neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits with transversal gates that builds in this known information and learns only which errors occurred. Duet leverages three insights. First, each transversal gate moves an error to a fixed place, so the network exchanges features only between the sites that a gate connects. Second, a logical outcome propagates through Clifford gates exactly and linearly, so the network predicts only the flips that the errors of each layer cause and combines the layers by a soft XOR. Third, every circuit is built from the same few gates, so the network takes the gates of each layer as input and one network per code distance decodes circuits of different sizes and depths. We pair Duet with the search decoder Tesseract, which re-decodes the few shots on which the network is least confident. On general circuits with 2 to 4 blocks and up to 16 layers, Duet alone is already more accurate than matching at every distance, and with Tesseract it fails 44 times less often than LoMatching at distance 9. On the random circuits of the Lukin group, it fails 0.299 times as often as their neural decoder at distance 7. The composition stays fast and takes 2.4 to 121.7 {\mu}s per layer, less than their network takes per gate at every distance.

nominations.title: Scaling Limits of Time-averaged Distributions for Symmetric Quantum Walks on Hypercubes
nominations.authors: Yusuke Ide, Norio Konno, Shuhei Mano
nominations.abstract: We study continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walks on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^d$ associated with symmetric random walks, that is, random walks whose transition probabilities depend only on the Hamming distance, using the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials. For continuous-time walks, we show that the time-averaged distribution of the Hamming distance is a discrete arcsine law whenever the eigenvalues are distinct. For discrete-time walks, exact formulas for the time-averaged distribution are known as combinatorial sums or as mixtures involving Krawtchouk polynomials, but their scaling limits as $d\to\infty$ (time average first) have not been specified. We obtain them explicitly for three random walks: the simple random walk (an arcsine law), the random walk with binomial weights (an equal mixture of arcsine laws with different supports), and the independent random walk (atoms of mass $1/2$ at $0$ and at $1/2$). Comparing with the continuous-time limits, the two models agree for the simple random walk but differ for the other two, so the correspondence between them is not universal.

nominations.title: Probing the inner structure of bound states
nominations.authors: Yahui Chai, Yibin Guo, Karl Jansen
nominations.abstract: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type. Taking the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, we find that fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses. At small masses, two classes of four-fermion operators play important but very different roles: the four fermion operators with two fermions and 2 anti-fermions at small distance give little improvement. In contrast, spatially extended meson-meson operators produce a large gain in state fidelity. Turning to observables, we find that the scalar charge is much more sensitive to the meson-meson operators than e.g. the meson mass. The parton distribution function (PDF) also changes from symmetric to asymmetric about the momentum fraction 1/2, along with the growing importance of meson-meson operators. These results establish QSE as a tool for probing the internal structure of composite particles and connecting it to observable properties.

nominations.title: Symmetry-constrained order hierarchy of connected optical responses in a five-level Rydberg-EIT medium
nominations.authors: Lintian Luo, Weixuan Gu, Yan Li
nominations.abstract: Determining the connected many-body correlations required for a nonlinear optical response of a given order is a central challenge in interacting open quantum systems. We establish a symmetrybased selection rule for connected optical responses in a driven-dissipative Rydberg-EIT model. Under the specified Lindblad conditions, local phase covariance and zero-probe factorization imply that an n-atom connected contribution to the root optical coherence is forbidden below probe-amplitude order 2n-1. Consequently, optical-response coefficients through fifth order involve at most three-atom connected clusters, without assuming weak interatomic interactions. Direct finite-cluster calculations confirm the predicted lowest allowed orders, while an illustrative Maxwell-propagation calculation shows that triplet contributions can partially oppose pair-induced polarization rotation. Our results establish a rigorous connection between optical perturbation order and the connected many-body sectors that can contribute to it.

nominations.title: Exact approach to double- and triple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems
nominations.authors: X. S. Sun, H. T. Cui, Y. A. Yan, H. Z. Shen
nominations.abstract: The determination of multiple-excitation bound state in open quantum systems is of broad interest in quantum physics. While the emergence of double- or triple-excitation bound state has been demonstrated in certain specific situations, their universality and exact solvability remain elusive. In this work, we present an exact approach to the double- or triple-excitation dynamics for interacting quantum emitters coupled to environment by deriving a closed equation. By this exact equation, we identify the critical condition for the emergence of double- or triple-excitation bound state, as well as its relationship to the single-excitation one. Our study not only clearly demonstrates the universality of double- or triple-excitation bound state in open quantum emitter systems, but also reveals the possibility of mediating inter-emitter interactions via multiple-excitation bound states.

nominations.title: From outcome exclusion to measurement simulation
nominations.authors: Kensei Torii, Jiaxi Kuang, Francesco Buscemi
nominations.abstract: While quantum state exclusion has received considerable attention, the analogous task of measurement outcome exclusion remains less explored. Here we develop a quantitative description of outcome exclusion and extend the resulting framework to obtain necessary and sufficient criteria for measurement simulation by quantum pre-processing and classical post-processing. Our analysis combines two approaches. Algebraic exclusion indices quantify normalized minimum errors in communication tasks with forbidden outputs and yield lower bounds on the number of classical messages required to reproduce the task statistics. Random exclusion profiles provide a statistical description in terms of optimized hypothesis-testing errors and are monotone under both types of processing. This connects outcome exclusion with statistical comparison in the spirit of Blackwell, linking the ability to suppress measurement outcomes to the possibility of simulating one measurement from another.

nominations.title: The Industrialization of Noise: Why Automated Proof-Solving is the Same Old Dead End
nominations.authors: Richard DeMillo, Richard Lipton
nominations.abstract: Nearly fifty years ago, DeMillo, Lipton, and Perlis argued that mathematical proofs are not static, isolated structures of formal logic, but the products of a vibrant, evolving social process of human critique, internalization, and shared intuition. In October 2026, OpenAI challenged this thesis by releasing a massive repository of 722 automated mathematical manuscripts, claiming full or partial solutions to 372 longstanding open problems. This paper examines the immediate crisis through the lens of the original DLP framework. We argue that the sudden, automated overproduction of dense, unreadable proofs represents an industrial pollution of the mathematical ecosystem. By examining the three fatal structural pillars of this automated approach (Specification, Regress, and Utility), we demonstrate that decoupling the act of mechanical solving from the human social process of understanding produces a sterile repository of dead logical artifacts. The resulting industrialization of unexamined manuscripts is self-fulfilling. Flooding the literature guarantees that the finite supply of human attention will lose the race to separate signal from noise. In this sense, posting a result is not the same act as submitting it to the community processes by which mathematics is vetted, digested, and incorporated into shared knowledge.

nominations.title: Information Security Risk Preparedness in Electronic Data Interchange: A Comparative Assessment of General IT and Healthcare Environments
nominations.authors: Naresh Kshetri, Bishwo Prakash Pokharel, Arati Bastakoti, Anjana Bastakoti
nominations.abstract: Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) supports the exchange of structured information across business and healthcare environments, making information security and organizational risk management critical to reliable digital transactions. This study empirically assesses security-control preparedness and organizational risk-taking ability in EDI-related environments through a comparative analysis of General IT Professionals (GIT) and Healthcare EDI Professionals (HEP). A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted with 100 respondents, equally divided between the two groups. Security Control Preparedness (SCP) and Threat Perception (TP) were validated using reliability and exploratory factor analyses, followed by group comparisons, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression. HEP respondents reported significantly higher SCP than GIT respondents (M = 4.70 vs. 3.89, p < 0.001, d = 1.06) and higher Organizational Risk-Taking Ability (ORTA) (M = 6.14 vs. 5.28, p = 0.001, d = 0.66). In contrast, GIT respondents reported higher threat perception (M = 2.95 vs. 2.04, p < 0.001, d = 0.72). SCP was positively associated with ORTA (r = 0.479, p < 0.001), whereas TP showed a significant negative association (r = -0.610, p < 0.001). A parsimonious regression model incorporating SCP and TP explained 41.6% of the variance in ORTA (R^2 = 0.416, adjusted R^2 = 0.404, p < 0.001). Based on these empirical findings, an EDI Risk Management Framework (EDI-RMF) is proposed integrating governance, human and organizational security, technical safeguards, physical protection, and continuous monitoring. The findings provide empirical evidence for strengthening information-security risk management in EDI-enabled environments, particularly within developing-economy contexts.

nominations.title: Towards Efficient Attack Tree Generation from Attack Graphs for Unobservable Target Analysis
nominations.authors: Chijioke Eze, Aliyu Tanko Ali, Leonard Chidiebere Eze, Antonello Monti, Damas Gruska, Martin Leucker
nominations.abstract: Attack trees provide a structured approach to security analysis but traditionally require prior knowledge of the attacker's objective. In practice, this objective often remains hidden, even when some attacker actions are partially detected. This paper presents a methodology for generating attack trees without assuming a predefined target by modeling the threat environment as a constraint-weighted graph and applying temporal reachability analysis. The approach identifies probable attacker locations from partial observations and a time budget, carrying traversal cost as an attack-tree attribute. It then extracts target-oriented subgraphs that preserve feasible attack paths while eliminating irrelevant nodes. We demonstrate the framework across three scenarios: a single office building, a multi-building industrial complex, and a real IoT device-communication network recovered from the CICIoT2023 attack dataset. Compared with the baselines, our approach achieves a lower reduction factor while maintaining complete target preservation, substantially outperforming topology-only methods that ignore temporal constraints. We further perform a sensitivity analysis across 66 weight configurations, showing that target identification is stable when strategic value receives at least 20\% of the weight in the single building and at least 50\% in the multi-building complex, while additional experiments reveal sensitivity to perturbations of the underlying strategic-value prior.

nominations.title: Scoring Recovery-Time Agent Security: Proposals, Effects, and Retry Instructions
nominations.authors: Paul Deepakraj Retinraj
nominations.abstract: A timed-out tool write may be absent, committed, or still in flight. Evaluating an agent only on whether its goal exists can hide harmful recovery actions: auditing 12 supplied traces changes apparent completion from 10/12 to 8/12. We introduce an executable evaluation that separately records tool proposals, runtime decisions, and committed effects. In 3,456 model episodes, the original task wording produces only 39/576 valid recoveries when the initial write is absent; a combined clarification produces 576/576. A further 1,584 episodes test stronger attacks and separate the effect definition from the recovery recipe with three rollouts per absent-state cell. Definition alone yields 276/288 valid recoveries; recipe alone yields 288/288. For Luna, malicious text is associated with 11.1 percentage points fewer valid recoveries under both original and definition-only wording, an availability signal limited by shared tasks and templates. The stronger attacks produce no attempted unauthorized or changed-key action and no unsafe effect. A trajectory audit finds six original-key retries after observing pending status: five denied and one deduplicated. Bounded checks distinguish atomic key enforcement from a delayed-commit race; stale negative reads also invalidate the evidence gate. A separate Claude Code program adds 720 successful episodes: 288 under the original attacks and 432 stronger-attack calibration episodes across Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku 5.5, with no observed proposal or effect deviations. The contribution is a measurement design and a diagnosis of availability, specification, and contract sensitivity, with no demonstrated general defense efficacy.

nominations.title: Trustworthy Edge AI: Security, Privacy, and Resilience for Distributed Intelligence
nominations.authors: Jaydip Sen, Subhasis Dasgupta
nominations.abstract: This chapter examines the principles and emerging research directions for building secure, privacy-preserving, and resilient Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) systems. As intelligence shifts from centralized clouds to distributed edge environments, challenges arise in ensuring data integrity, privacy, and reliable operation under adversarial and uncertain conditions. The chapter analyzes Edge AI architectures, emphasizing the expanded attack surface due to heterogeneous devices, resource constraints, and dynamic networks. It reviews core security mechanisms, including hardware-rooted trust, zero-trust models, secure communication, and attestation. Privacy-preserving approaches, such as federated learning, secure aggregation, and differential privacy, enable collaborative intelligence without centralized data sharing. Resilience strategies, including fault tolerance, adversarial robustness, and adaptive orchestration, are also explored. Case studies from smart cities, autonomous vehicles, healthcare, and industrial IoT illustrate practical trade-offs. The chapter advocates a holistic, cross-layer design integrating security, privacy, and resilience for trustworthy edge intelligence.

nominations.title: High Throughput Meets Low Latency: CKKS Functional Bootstrapping on GPUs
nominations.authors: Carlos Agull\'o-Domingo, Carlo Pascoe, \'Oscar Vera-L\'opez, Andreea Alexandru, Ahmad Al Badawi, Jos\'e L. Abell\'an, Yuriy Polyakov
nominations.abstract: Functional (programmable) bootstrapping extends the bootstrapping operation of Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to evaluate an arbitrary function while refreshing a ciphertext. This capability was a unique feature of scalar CGGI/DM cryptosystems for many years until it was recently added to the toolset of vectorized FHE schemes, with CKKS being the most promising option both in terms of throughput (amortized time) and functionality. Previous work showed that CKKS functional bootstrapping outperforms CGGI/DM functional bootstrapping in terms of throughput by two to three orders of magnitude, but still loses in latency on CPU by two to three orders of magnitude. We present an optimized GPU implementation of CKKS functional bootstrapping that closes the latency gap. Our implementation supports evaluating functions over both small integers (as in CGGI/DM) and real numbers (unique to CKKS), which we call discrete-CKKS and continuous-CKKS functional bootstrapping, respectively.

nominations.title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests
nominations.authors: Karthik Karunanithi
nominations.abstract: Runtime controls for tool-using agents depend on manifests that state what each tool may read and where its output may go. Evaluations of these controls, including ChainCaps, report per-attack blocking: the share of attacks a set of manifests stops. We show that this is the wrong unit. A catalog is only as safe as its weakest source policy: if $M$ independently authored policies are each wrong with probability $p$, the chance that the catalog contains an accepted exfiltration path is $1-(1-p)^M$, while per-attack blocking stays at $1-p$. Three lines of evidence agree. In synthetic catalogs run through two enforcement engines, ChainCaps and OpenAPPA, per-attack blocking holds at 92% while catalog vulnerability rises from 22% at 10 tools to 99% at 200, and composition provides no protective effect. A fifteen-model authoring pilot shows that real errors cluster by author, so a 200-tool catalog behaves like about 5 independent decisions rather than 60 (95% interval 3.4 to 9.2). On 114 real MCP tools with expert-written rules, the models' own manifests block 89% of attacks yet leave 9 of 15 catalogs open, as the author-effect model predicts and independence does not. Evaluations should report catalog vulnerability, the sink coverage of their tests, and an effective number of independent decisions alongside per-attack blocking.

nominations.title: Leaks by Installments: Cross-Session Answer Disclosure in LLM Tutors and a Ledger-Based Defense
nominations.authors: Venkata Muttineni, Karthik Narayan, Christopher David
nominations.abstract: Tutors built on large language models (LLMs) are told not to give away answers, but a learner does not have to ask for the answer all at once. Existing safeguards judge each reply within the current conversation, so a learner can open a new session, reword the problem, or request a worked solution to the same problem with different numbers. We call this cross-session disclosure and propose a defense: a persistent, per-learner disclosure ledger. For every problem a learner brings, the system builds a typed solution graph. Before a reply is released, a gate matches the reply's own content, not the learner's wording, against the ledger by result values and by type-labeled solution structure, then computes which steps the learner could now derive. The reply is withheld if that set reaches the final answer or exceeds a budget. In a simulation of 3,000 problems, the ledger reduced leakage through renumbered practice variants from 100% to 10.6% while honest learners completed 94-99.5% of problems. With two real LLM tutors (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Phi-3.5-mini-instruct) on 60 problems, leakage through renumbered variants fell from 0.58 to 0.08 and from 1.00 to 0.18, with 98% honest completion. The ledger did not reduce split requests beyond a per-session gate in the live runs. All acceptance criteria were fixed before each run.

nominations.title: The Fingerprinting Paradox: Why Sensitivity Undermines Black-Box Model Integrity Verification
nominations.authors: Shahinul Hoque, Farhin Farhad Riya, Jinyuan Sun, Fnu Suya
nominations.abstract: Black-box integrity verification aims to detect unauthorized modifications to outsourced models using only prediction APIs. Existing frameworks seek to improve verification efficiency through sensitive fingerprints: queries whose predictions are more likely to change under tampering than those of genuine inputs. We show that this sensitivity can also help dishonest providers recognize verification queries and selectively conceal tampering. We prove that excess sensitivity relative to genuine inputs lower-bounds statistical distinguishability. We evaluate five integrity verification frameworks across three model architectures, three datasets, and three adversarial knowledge settings. When the deployed framework is known, our fingerprint detectors achieve AUCs at least 0.989, and selective filtering makes all five frameworks require significantly larger estimated query budgets than genuine inputs, reversing their intended efficiency advantage. A query-efficiency advantage remains marginally in a small subset of evaluated settings with poor detection transfer. We further design verification methods under stronger concealment constraints but find that reduced detectability comes with losses in sensitivity or fingerprint-generation success. Our results expose a sensitivity-detectability tension and show that sensitivity alone does not ensure efficient black-box verification against adaptive malicious providers.

nominations.title: Where Agent Defenses Fail: A Case Study of Policy Compositions and Measurement Limits
nominations.authors: Kunwar Singh Sangram, Krishna Mohan Guda Nagavenkata Srinivasa
nominations.abstract: A coding agent may need to upload a report while its sandbox blocks network access. A host mediator can restore delivery, but an injected instruction may add a secret to the approved request. We study this interaction using files and HTTP receipts to measure effects independently of control logs. Two prospective frozen-input cohorts comprise 110 and 300 runs on previously explored authored tasks. Restrictive sandboxing produces no observed attack harm but reduces benign utility to 6/8 and 12/24. Mediation restores uploads and admits disclosure; complete-line matching retains full benign utility but misses two value-only disclosures in the expanded cohort. A separate 72-run boundary study identifies encoded disclosure, observer misses, and formatting checks that obscure benign refusals. An 80-run SafeAgents/OpenShell follow-up shows that containment stops the tested guard misses among valid observations, while mediation restores benign uploads and delivers both encoded-attestation attacks. Twelve judge-error rows remain unscored. A separate response-capture diagnostic reproduces their failures at the native token budget. A 12-run exact-publication-contract experiment blocks both attacks but also rejects both benign formatting variants; a 4-run normalized follow-up restores both benign uploads while still rejecting both attacks. These small, single-model studies identify delivery-path and measurement limits; they do not establish general attack resistance.

nominations.title: Aftershock: Yesterday's Linux Kernel Bugs, Tomorrow's Android Exploits
nominations.authors: Kareem Shehada, Zhiyun Qian
nominations.abstract: Android kernels have long suffered from slow patch propagation from Linux upstream, with fixes often reaching devices far later than conventional Linux distributions. Until recently, this lag was largely a patch-management problem. With rapidly improving LLM agents, it is becoming an exploitation problem: public upstream patches can now serve as blueprints for building working n-day exploits before downstream devices are fixed. We test this threat end to end by building an automated pipeline that screens upstream Linux patches, reproduces memory-safety vulnerabilities on Android targets, and drives an LLM agent to construct local privilege escalation exploits from an untrusted application. Across 152 candidate CVEs reported over 33 months, we reproduce 38 vulnerabilities and generate 17 independently verified exploits under production defenses. Exploitation takes a median of 14.3 agent-hours and $321 in API cost, with 90% median reliability; 12 of 14 trials succeed on Pixel 9 and Pixel 10 devices. Notably, the pipeline relies only on publicly available, off-the-shelf models. Surprisingly, only 3 of the 17 exploited CVEs appear in Android Security Bulletins, suggesting limited visibility into which upstream fixes address vulnerabilities that affect Android kernels. For these 17 CVEs, the corresponding upstream patches reach Pixel devices with a median delay of 181 days. Together, these results reveal a stark asymmetry: attackers can increasingly automate exploitation in hours, while defenders still identify and deploy fixes on the timescale of months.

nominations.title: Evaluating LLM Security Review Agents with Operationally Sourced Ground Truth
nominations.authors: Mudita Khurana, Karim Liman-Tinguiri
nominations.abstract: LLM-based security review agents can reason about vulnerabilities that deterministic tools miss, but deploying them responsibly requires knowing whether they actually work. Existing benchmarks construct ground truth synthetically or from public CVE databases and are blind to the vulnerability patterns specific to a given production codebase. We present an evaluation framework grounded in an organisation's own vulnerabilities, with three contributions. First, a dataset construction methodology that derives ground truth from operational security data (bug bounty reports, penetration test findings and internally reported vulnerabilities), exploiting the property that a confirmed vulnerability must exist immediately before its fix is merged and be absent immediately after. Second, two complementary evaluation strategies: one reviewing the pull request that introduced a vulnerability and one searching a repository where it already exists. Both run through a two-agent pipeline pairing a Security Engineer agent, which reviews code without knowledge of the vulnerability, with a Judge agent that decides whether its findings would have mitigated the known issue. Third, a trace-level behavioural characterisation of how frontier models reason about these vulnerabilities. Across GPT-5.5, Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5 shows higher discovery rates on the pull-request strategy (57%, 95% CI [42%, 72%]) after a round of OPRO-style improvements, and Sonnet 4.6 on the repository strategy (69%, 95% CI [56%, 81%]). Trace analysis shows the models have complementary strengths that explain these differences, and that outcome-only scoring can mischaracterise their production behaviour. The methodology relies only on artefacts that vulnerability management workflows commonly produce, though all results come from a single organisation's codebase and we have not tested how well they generalise.

nominations.title: Internal inconsistencies and unresolved experimental evidence in a quantum neurosecurity framework
nominations.authors: S. Grigorovich, M. Bairachnaya, E. Daroczi, J. Marshall, B. Giros
nominations.abstract: This article presents a technical and theoretical assessment of the Quantum-Entangled Neuro-Symbolic Swarm Federation (QENSSF), a framework intended for privacy-preserving, quantum-secure, AI-powered, multimodal healthcare data analysis, introduced by Ben Othman and Ali (2025). They claim QENSSF is a first-in-class framework with provable privacy and security guarantees, support these with theorems and proofs, report an experimental evaluation on IBM's quantum Eagle processor, report a real-world quantum key distribution (QKD) test, and claim use of real-world multimodal datasets (ADNI, UK Biobank, and MIMIC-IV). Our examination of quantitative support for these claims identified various concerns. Most importantly, the security criterion of a central guarantee (Theorem 1) cannot be satisfied given the risk formulation and relevant constraints, which, along with calculation errors in the proof, directly undermines the claim of provable security. Furthermore, insufficient reporting of biomedical datasets and unresolved discrepancies in the hardware evaluation limit verification of the experimental claims and overall reproducibility. QENSSF identifies a real need: ensuring privacy and security of healthcare data while patients benefit from AI-powered analysis. This need is particularly pressing for sensitive neural data, including the neuroimaging data available through sources such as ADNI. Privacy concerns also extend to wearable EEG data, for which reidentification risks can persist despite deidentification. However, QENSSF's foundational inconsistencies need resolution before it could be considered in the neurosecurity domain.

nominations.title: Open-Set Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification with Feature Fusion and Vision Transformer
nominations.authors: Jie Ma, Junqing Zhang, Guanxiong Shen, Linning Peng, Alan Marshall
nominations.abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) is a promising device authentication technique for the Internet of Things (IoT) that leverages hardware impairments to uniquely identify devices. However, most existing RFFI systems operate under a closed-set assumption and lack the ability to detect rogue devices, which poses significant security risks. In this paper, we propose an open-set RFFI approach that jointly performs rogue device detection and legitimate device classification. Specifically, we designed a multi-task RFFI system that integrates an autoencoder (AE) for rogue device detection and a fully connected (FC) layer for classification. To enrich the feature representation, we generated two channel-independent spectrograms (CISs) with distinct window lengths from the I/Q signals, capturing complementary time-frequency characteristics. These CISs were processed in parallel by two Vision Transformer (ViT) networks, and their outputs were fused via feature concatenation to construct a device fingerprint for both tasks. We built a testbed involving ten legitimate LoRa devices and five rogue devices. We conducted a comprehensive experimental evaluation and compared our approach with several benchmark algorithms. Experimental results show that our fused feature multi-task RFFI consistently outperformed the baselines in both legitimate device classification and rogue device detection. Our proposed approach achieved an accuracy of 91.1% and an area under the curve (AUC) of over 0.72 in a realistic wireless scenario where the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was 20 to 30 dB.

nominations.title: Harvesting Apple's Orchard: A Security Analysis of On-Device CoreML Models Across the Apple Ecosystem
nominations.authors: Justice Owusu Agyemang, Winifred Harriet Asante, Kwame Opuni-Boachie Obour Agyekum, Kwame Agyeman-Prempeh Agyekum, Francisca Adoma Acheampong, Jerry John Kponyo
nominations.abstract: Apple ships hundreds of task-specific machine-learning models inside iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS. We present, to our knowledge, the first systematic security analysis of this on-device surface. We harvested 1,137 CoreML artifacts from six platform images and two device harvests, and a conversion pipeline recovered 155 previously opaque bundles as loadable mlpackage archives. Eight findings. (1) 368 of 1,137 artifacts expose plaintext learned parameters (281 blobs, 369.61 MiB) and 166 of 166 MIL bundles leak internal model-database tokens. (2) Specification versions 1-9 coexist and locale variants diverge architecturally. (3) Across 82,092 adversarial evaluations (221 model paths), worst-case flip rates reach 100%; zero-width spaces flip 65% of the Indian-English and 70% of the US-English SMS filter. (4) A 16-byte weight edit flips 7 of 8 probe inputs of a system model, with no runtime integrity check observed. (5) Loading Apple's own hand-gesture model crashes libBNNS through the public CoreML API (4/4 on production M2, also macOS 27.0); Apple ruled it a self-crash outside the security boundary. (6) Eleven bundles ship isUpdatable=1 hooks. (7) SMS text-classifier latency is 13.1-52.0 ms, 92.4% in the CPU-side NLP core, not the ANE. (8) The classifiers label 8-9 of 10 phishing messages Transactional. We filed three reports with Apple Product; all were declined as not crossing a security boundary, and we report the findings as robustness results.

nominations.title: SigK: rPPG-based key agreement scheme for mHealth
nominations.authors: Yanping Wang, Lin Li, Leo Yu Zhang, Jianfeng Wang, Chao Chen, Kok-Leong Ong, Jun Zhang
nominations.abstract: As mobile health advances, the use of biomedical sensors for disease monitoring, diagnosis, and treatment is increasing. These sensors often need to be connected through wireless communication technologies to process physiological information from various body parts effectively. Since the data transmitted in these devices usually contain sensitive personal medical information, it is crucial to establish secure communication between devices. In recent studies, the inter-pulse intervals between heartbeats are often used as the key source. They can be extracted from physiological signals such as photoplethysmogram (PPG) or electrocardiogram (ECG), allowing key agreement schemes without pre-key distribution. However, traditional solutions are based on contact measurement devices (e.g., wristbands, chest straps), which limit their applicability in contactless healthcare scenarios. In this paper, we propose a remote PPG-based key agreement scheme to facilitate secure communication between contactless medical devices. We leverage medical devices equipped with cameras to capture remote PPG signals from human faces, and then utilize the signal's power spectral density and peak-peak interval to establish a key agreement with signals synchronously acquired in the Body Area Network (BAN). We have carried out performance evaluations on three publicly available datasets to demonstrate the feasibility of our proposed scheme. In addition, we have also presented a comprehensive proof of the security of our proposed scheme.

nominations.title: Mixed-Initiative Mining of Root-Cause Analyses into Audit Priors for C/C++ Vulnerability Hunting
nominations.authors: Yuhei Kawakoya, Eitaro Shioji, Yuto Otsuki, Makoto Iwamura
nominations.abstract: Vulnerability auditing of large C/C++ codebases is constrained by limited review attention. Human auditors and LLM-based agents need operational priors that indicate where to look first and what to suspect, but such priors are rarely available in directly usable form. Rather than proposing a new vulnerability detector, we derive audit-steering artifacts from evidence-backed root-cause analysis (RCA) reports. We introduce two complementary representations: Occurrence Context (OC), a location prior based on file role, function role, and data-structure class; and Vulnerability-Inducing Structural Patterns (VISP), reusable failure-mechanism priors. OC guides where to inspect, while VISP guides what to suspect. On 108 CVEs from Vul4C, OC's parser-based priority ranking, without LLM inference, outperforms generic prioritization baselines with moderate-to-large effect sizes. Packaged as executable SKILLs, OC and VISP form a dual-SKILL workflow that improves audit-relevant broad coverage, defined as match-or-partial findings within ground-truth functions that share the patch's failure mechanism, as assessed by three LLM judges. Across the 108-CVE cohort, dual-SKILL improves function-level broad matches by 5.3 percentage points; gains reach 7.2 points on mid-size projects and 15.0 points on large (1500-4999-line) vulnerable files. These results suggest that RCA-derived priors help direct limited audit attention toward vulnerable code. The agent-coverage evaluation is a single-run operational probe, with one run per commit, characterizing the direction and scale of the effect rather than its precise magnitude.

nominations.title: HDMark: Holographic Multi-Bit Model Watermarking for Intellectual Property Protection in Hyperdimensional Computing
nominations.authors: Hamed Poursiami, Ahmad Tahmasivand, Farshad Soleiman, Guojing Cong, Thomas Potok, Kai Zeng, Khaled N. Khasawneh, Maryam Parsa
nominations.abstract: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) models deployed on edge hardware are valuable intellectual property that is easy to steal, since a trained classifier consolidates its learned knowledge into a compact set of class prototype hypervectors; yet protecting their ownership through watermarking remains largely unexplored. We present HDMark, the first model watermarking framework native to HDC, which encodes ownership in the same hyperdimensional algebra the model computes with. HDMark maps a multi-bit owner identity to secret quasi-orthogonal carriers, superimposes them holographically onto the trained class prototypes, and verifies ownership with a statistical test. Across four datasets and three HDC learning rules, HDMark leaves accuracy essentially unchanged and verifies a 64-bit identity in 99.8% of trials at p < 0.001. We derive closed-form expressions for prediction fidelity and bit recovery that match measurements within 0.4 pp mean absolute error. The watermark survives fine-tuning and low-bit quantization, while attempting to erase it through noise injection, pruning, or overwriting severely degrades model accuracy. We further identify a dimension-permutation attack specific to HDC, which reorders hypervector coordinates to evade verification without altering predictions, and counter it through encoder realignment. Finally, an AMD ZCU104 FPGA implementation confirms that HDMark adds no hardware overhead, remains bit-exact under aggressive undervolting, and stays verifiable under timing faults until the classifier itself fails.

nominations.title: SwarmLeak: Does Coordination Improve Privacy Attacks on LLM Agents?
nominations.authors: Asma Farajidizaji, Vyas Raina, Vatsal Raina, Ivaxi Sheth
nominations.abstract: LLM agents increasingly collaborate in group chats while holding tool access to confidential records, which makes the shared chat an attack surface. It remains unclear whether several colluding attackers extract such information more effectively than one. We introduce SwarmLeak, a red-teaming dataset of 24 synthetic group-chat scenarios across healthcare, law, finance, and software engineering, where attackers pose as colleagues to make a victim agent post protected fields despite an explicit confidentiality policy. With GLM 5.2 attacking five victim models through seven conversational strategies, we compare one attacker with a swarm of four sharing a private channel, matching scenarios, strategies, and a 200,000-token budget that also covers swarm coordination. Swarms show no advantage: a single attacker matches or exceeds them on every victim, and the share of runs leaking any field differs between conditions by at most 14.3 percentage points, whereas changing the victim shifts it from 0% to 99.4%. On the two most vulnerable models, nearly every run leaks under both conditions, but single attackers expose more of the record at first disclosure (85.4% vs. 68.1% of protected fields on Nemotron 3.5 Lightning). Four of the five victims leaked despite the policy. GLM 5.2 retrieved protected data in 64.3% of individual-attack runs and leaked in 0.6%: retrieval does not imply disclosure, but in high-stakes settings even one leaked field can identify a patient or client. At equal budgets, a larger red team is not automatically a stronger one; the victim model matters far more.
